question: Should OpenClaw add a `HEARTBEAT.md` task-level model metadata contract, or should this be handled through a broader per-turn/model-router API or plugin hook design?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe implementation depends on maintainer intent for public syntax, whether due tasks split into separate turns, and how model overrides interact with provider auth, fallbacks, and session state.

options.title: Design shared routing contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose a reusable per-turn or scheduled-work routing contract that covers heartbeat and related cron needs.

options.title: Add heartbeat-only task metadata
options.body: Implement a narrow `HEARTBEAT.md` task model field with explicit split/group semantics and compatibility tests.

options.title: Route to plugin-only policy
options.body: Decline core task syntax and document that whole-turn routing should use `before_model_resolve`, accepting that multiple due tasks cannot be independently routed today.

recommendation.title: Design shared routing contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose a reusable per-turn or scheduled-work routing contract that covers heartbeat and related cron needs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model-hook and product-boundary history makes this the best available owner for choosing between core heartbeat syntax and a broader routing API.
